hints: Each new road merges two components or leaves connectivity unchanged.
DSU reports whether endpoints were in different components and the new component size after a merge.
Track the number of components and the largest component size after every road.
analogy: A road either joins two groups into a larger group or connects cities already in the same group.
example: Joining components of sizes 3 and 2 changes the component count by -1 and creates size 5.
algorithm: Initialize each city as a DSU component. For each edge, union its endpoints if distinct, update component count and maximum size, then print both.
correctness: DSU represents exactly the connected components after each insertion; merging only distinct roots changes the count once and sums their sizes.
complexity: O((n+m) alpha(n)) time and O(n) space, where alpha is the inverse Ackermann function.
